newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS COACH LIPPU SAYS TITLE RACE IS NOT OVER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS COACH LIPPU SAYS TITLE RACE IS NOT OVER.

text.p: Juventus coach Marcello Lippi rejects suggestions that his side have just about wrapped up the Italian title following their 0-0 top-of-the-table draw with Internazionale at the San Siro on Sunday.
"We've still got to battle to win the title and it won't be easy. Inter and Parma could both still catch us and they'll do everything possible to do so, I've no doubt", said Lippi.
With 10 games to play, Juventus lead by five points from second-placed Parma with Inter a further two points away in third.
But Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson disagreed with Lippi.
"This 0-0 draw means that Juventus have won the championship and that we are left to fight for second place," he said.
Hodgson's view was echoed by the Milan-based sports daily Gazzetta Dello Sport which praised Juventus for their attacking attitude in a difficult away game.
"Juventus could have decided to play safe...instead they came out to play, to finish off the business with a display of force and they came close to striking the knockout punch," it said.

The game was marked by a controversial decision by referee Pier Luigi Collina to overrule a ninth-minute goal by Inter striker Maurizio Ganz but many commentators pointed out that Juventus came close to scoring at least three times.
Inter's experienced captain Giuseppe Bergomi said the furore over the disallowed goal had affected his side.
"Unfortunately Collina's decision made us lose our cool and we spent the next half-hour being dominated by Juventus," he said.
"In the second half, you saw Inter at their best but obviously if we were going to open up the title contest again then we had to win."
On Saturday Juventus are at home to AS Roma and Inter travel to Parma for a direct clash for second place and participation in next season's European Champions' League.
Parma, 2-1 winners away to Perugia on Sunday, have overcome a dreadful start to the season, which saw them sink to 15th position at one stage, to emerge as the closest challenger to Juventus.
Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti, however, is keen to play down suggestions that Juventus have wrapped up the title.
"For the time being, Juventus seem different class from us...but, mind you, soccer sometimes defies all forecasts and previews," he said.
